doc.title: Eddie Miller and Pete Fountain Interview, 1970-01-09

title: Listening to the new album and Eddie's own records
summary: They play Spinning Wheel, discuss Eddie and Pete's duet lines, Glenn Campbell's record with Eddie, and a possible Eddie album.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: yeah he's quite a guy listen let's listen to one of these uh tracks from your new album right right spinning will ¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ ¶¶ Hurdy-gurdy kind of sound.
Not big, that's for sure. Well, no, it's a little flavor of Eddie Miller, of Pete Fountain.
The lines that you two play together, very interesting.
Yeah. We really enjoyed on that every night. We pick each other's skulls, you see. And he gets involved sometimes. Sometimes it's wrong, but it's more joy.

I don't know how many people are aware that Eddie made Glenn Campbell famous. He put Glenn on a record with him overnight, right? Six months, he was the number one star. That's true. That's right. Do you have another album in the works, Eddie?
Too bad. I think this thing is. Now, what an honest guy. Usually an artist says, well, not right now, but there'll be something coming out one of these days.

Oh, I think they will. I hope so. This came out real good with him. I guess when they find the right songs, as they say, they always tell you that. But we know them all. And we could, you know, like, they could do all the pretty songs of Eddie, you know, done through the years. And I think it'd be a fantastic album. You know, like Music for Lovers, because he can do it.
Stanley Dance calls Eddie the first of the cool tenors. Really?
Yeah. Well, that's quite a compliment from him.
